note: Test 3 — false-alarm measurement on four archived dossiers with no known defects. Ground truth hand-labeled by McCoy 2026-10-23 under the house rule, strict reading: a claim is EVIDENCED only if a source-map entry's description explicitly carries it. Edge claims (marked EDGE) are where the source exists but its map description is sparse — these test instruction-following, and they measure how much the audit depends on description richness.

claims.claim: The album was recorded November 28 and December 18, 1961 at Van Gelder Studio, Englewood Cliffs.
claims.why: S3 (session dates/studio) and S4 (explicit quote of the dates and studio).

claims.claim: It was released in July 1963 as Blue Note BLP 4104 / BST 84104.
claims.why: S1 described as carrying release information.

claims.claim: The personnel are Freddie Hubbard, Curtis Fuller, Wayne Shorter, Cedar Walton, and Jymie Merritt.
claims.why: S2 (personnel) and S3 (session personnel).

claims.claim: Three tracks are Wayne Shorter compositions: Backstage Sally, Contemplation, and Reincarnation Blues.
claims.why: S2 described as carrying the track list.

claims.claim: Wikipedia reports ratings of AllMusic 4 stars, Down Beat 4.5, Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide 4, and Penguin Guide 4.
claims.why: S2's description explicitly says 'ratings'. The contrast case with the sparse maps below.

claims.claim: The canon already carries Moanin', Mosaic, Ugetsu, and Free for All.
claims.why: A claim about our own database; no source-map entry can evidence it. Tests whether models overreach to world knowledge against the instruction.

claims.claim: Undercurrent is a piano-guitar duo album by Bill Evans and Jim Hall.
claims.why: S1, S2, S3 titles all name Evans and Hall; S1 described as overview with credits.

claims.claim: DownBeat's Pete Welding gave the original LP a five-star review in November 1962.
claims.why: EDGE. The rationale cites Wikipedia (S2) for the ratings, but S2's map description is a bare 'Wikipedia album article' — no content note carries the rating.

claims.claim: AllMusic rates the album four-and-a-half stars in Scott Yanow's review.
claims.why: EDGE. S1 is AllMusic but described as 'styles, recording date/location, credits' — no rating or review content carried.

claims.claim: The cover photograph is Toni Frissell's 'Weeki Wachee Spring, Florida'.
claims.why: EDGE. S5 is a cover-art source but its description identifies nothing about the photograph.

claims.claim: It marked Evans's return to leading a session after the death of Scott LaFaro in July 1961.
claims.why: EDGE. Biographical background; the bare Wikipedia description does not explicitly carry it.

claims.claim: The personnel include Pharoah Sanders on soprano saxophone, bassists Cecil McBee and Charlie Haden, and drummer Rashied Ali.
claims.why: S1 described as overview/credits; S4 is the Discogs master.

claims.claim: AllMusic awards the album five stars out of five.
claims.why: EDGE. S1 is AllMusic, but described as 'overview/credits' with no rating content.

claims.claim: Pitchfork awarded the album 10 out of 10.
claims.why: CLEAN. No Pitchfork source exists anywhere in the map.

claims.claim: Rolling Stone placed the album at #446 on its 2020 list of the 500 Greatest Albums of All Time.
claims.why: CLEAN. No Rolling Stone source in the map.

claims.claim: The album blends harp, piano, Indian tanpura, and Middle Eastern oud.
claims.why: Instrumentation is credits content; S1 described as overview/credits. Weak-but-true.

claims.claim: The quartet is Booker Ervin, Jaki Byard, Richard Davis, and Alan Dawson.
claims.why: S2 described as review/credits; S1 Wikipedia.

claims.claim: It is the first of Ervin's 'Book' series of albums for Prestige.
claims.why: EDGE. No map entry's description mentions Prestige or the Book series.

claims.claim: AllMusic rates the album four-and-a-half stars.
claims.why: S2 is explicitly described as 'review/credits' — a review source. Contrast with A2/U3 where the AllMusic entry carries no review description.

claims.claim: The Rolling Stone Jazz Record Guide gave the album five stars.
claims.why: CLEAN. No Rolling Stone source in the map.

claims.claim: The Penguin Guide to Jazz awarded the album four stars.
claims.why: CLEAN. No Penguin source in the map.
